title: Z-section floor beam: unsymmetric bending
who: Stress engineers sizing floor beams, stringers and frames (Z and angle sections are everywhere in airframes)
why_hard: A Z-section has a non-zero product of inertia, so a vertical moment bends it about an inclined neutral axis. The peak stress (22,200 psi at the web-flange corners) is twice what sigma = My/I gives (11,100 psi), and the tip of the 'compressed' top flange is actually in TENSION (+11,100 psi). Using My/I halves the peak stress and gets the sign wrong at the flange tips.
failure_cost: A 2x unconservative bending stress; wrong-sign stresses also corrupt crippling and fatigue checks at the flange tips.
sources: Megson, Aircraft Structures for Engineering Students, Ch. 16 (unsymmetrical bending, Z-section example)
Bruhn, Section A5 (bending of unsymmetrical sections)
